title: CS1-SAB with an absorbed envelope E and heralded tolerance 1 - 1/m^4

claims.statement: For every integer N >= 2 and s in Z/NZ, put n = ceil(log2 N). The single CS1-SAB algorithm in proof.md recovers the whole s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3 from independent ideal coset copies. On EVERY branch, including failures, retries, discards and aborts, total charged sequential work is T = O(n^(7/2) 2^(sqrt(2n))) (proof.md (13.6)), hence T = O(E(n)), where E(n) = 2^(a sqrt(n) - sum_(i=1..28) k_i n^(1/2) (log2 n)^(-1/(10^256 - i))), with k_1 = ... = k_27 = 10^256 - 1, k_28 = 10^58 - 1, and a = u_333/v_333 > sqrt(2) the exact Pell rational of proof.md Section 0 (the same coefficient appears verbatim in the structured object, which lists E term by term). Lemma 14.1 of proof.md (absorption, using only a - sqrt(2) > 0) proves that n^P 2^(sqrt(2n)) = O(E(n)) for every fixed P. Under the heralded malformed-copy model of claim 4 (proof.md Sections 11.1, 13.5 and 15), where the algorithm runs FILTER with the literal raw cutoff D Qcap* (D = m^4; Qcap* = Qcap on the main branch and N(n+10) on the finite branch), the displayed big-O bound and the declared envelope still hold on every branch. All four resource bounds and tolerance hold jointly for the same configuration, with absolute outside constants. The declared envelope is E(n); its exact growth index is 1/2.

The single CS1-SAB algorithm in proof.md recovers the whole s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3 from independent ideal coset copies. On EVERY branch, including failures, retries, discards and aborts, fresh source acquisitions, including every discarded and rejected copy, are at most the explicit Qcap = O(n^(5/4) 2^(sqrt(2n) - 16 (2n)^(1/4))) on the main branch (proof.md (13.2)) and N(n+10) on the finite branch, hence Q = O(E(n)), where E(n) = 2^(a sqrt(n) - sum_(i=1..28) k_i n^(1/2) (log2 n)^(-1/(10^256 - i))), with k_1 = ... = k_27 = 10^256 - 1, k_28 = 10^58 - 1, and a = u_333/v_333 > sqrt(2) the exact Pell rational of proof.md Section 0 (the same coefficient appears verbatim in the structured object, which lists E term by term). Lemma 14.1 of proof.md (absorption, using only a - sqrt(2) > 0) proves that n^P 2^(sqrt(2n)) = O(E(n)) for every fixed P. Under the heralded malformed-copy model of claim 4 (proof.md Sections 11.1, 13.5 and 15), where the algorithm runs FILTER with the literal raw cutoff D Qcap* (D = m^4), raw acquisitions are at most D Qcap on the main branch and D N(n+10) on the finite branch; this is again O(n^(5/4) 2^(sqrt(2n) - 16 (2n)^(1/4))) and O(E(n)) on every branch, while the literal caps Qcap and N(n+10) stated above apply to the clean problem and to the well-formed copies used. The same CS1-SAB configuration, with the heralded filter FILTER of proof.md Section 11.1 (literal raw-acquisition cutoff D Qcap*, with D = m^4 and Qcap* = Qcap on the main branch, N(n+10) on the finite branch), proves fractional error tolerance epsilon(n) = 9994611312796487755881848654079456777805183045569497927783747881*9994611312796487755881848654079456777805183045569497927783747883*9999999999999999999999999906587220629241422304506584841132897669*9989225529387953241424683186546005111325213024773532711531961825/9994611312796487755881848654079456777805183045569497927783747882^4 = 1 - 1/m^4, a constant in (0,1), where m, F and G are the integers of proof.md Section 15 (F G = m^2 + 1 by the Brahmagupta-Fibonacci identity). Under the stated heralded malformed-copy model, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), if at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed on every branch, the algorithm outputs the entire s with probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3, and the four resource bounds of claims 0-3 hold jointly on every execution branch in the form stated there for the heralded model. With no malformed copies (the clean problem, no herald) the algorithm is the clean algorithm. No positive tolerance is claimed for undetectable corruptions.

structured.error_model: Heralded malformed-copy model with fraction epsilon(n). Parameters: N >= 2 is the modulus, s in Z/NZ the secret, n = ceil(log2 N), Q the total number of source copies the algorithm acquires on an execution branch, and epsilon(n) the tolerated malformed fraction. Each acquired copy consists of an (n+1)-qubit register of the ideal copy's shape together with one classical herald bit f delivered with it. Copies are delivered one at a time in acquisition order j = 1, ..., Q. Before copy j is delivered, an adversary that knows N, s, the full description of the algorithm and every measurement outcome the algorithm obtained before copy j is delivered, and that may hold, process and measure an arbitrary private quantum system, decides adaptively whether copy j is malformed. A well-formed copy has f = 0 and its register is a fresh copy of rho_s, in tensor product with every other system (earlier copies, the adversary's system and the algorithm's registers). A malformed copy has f = 1 and its register is in an arbitrary state chosen by the adversary, possibly entangled with the adversary's private system and with other malformed copies. On every execution branch at most floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the Q acquired copies are malformed. The herald is always correct, so malformation is detectable (an erasure-type error); its timing, its number within the promise and the malformed register contents are adversarial. In the clean problem no herald is supplied and every copy is well-formed. No source control, purification access or preparation inverse is supplied.
